limitations: the working-set lease release is NOT observed by name in this run: no `DIAG,ws_release` row. That row is emitted only where the release path fires -- a take-start sweep (which excludes the capturing track, so a same-track sequence never sweeps its own slots), the memory-pressure release, or the playback-reset/undo path. Its absence means this run did not exercise it, not that the release failed; the release remains exercised natively (S4.3's reuse fixture).

L5 is identity-grade: the bind is read from `DIAG,reentry,bound,<tick>,<interval>,<slot>,<depth>`, which names the same `captureInterval_` the denial names. (The earlier claim that nothing names that identity on the binding edge is withdrawn -- it described the state before this change added the `bound` record.) The *release* marker is separate and is NOT the availability edge: it is emitted on the first maintenance turn at which the resources were observed free, which is measurably later than the admission it enables.

L7 note-level evidence: `storedNoteEvent`/`storedNotes` have no callers, so the capture has no per-note record of its own. Pitch-level proof therefore comes from the content pipeline's `!CAPTURE_CONTENT` dump (`--content-dump`), whose `begin` row names the dumped slot and whose events carry real pitches, plus `content-review.json` (`--content-review`) for storage<->effective parity. Note the dump's own oddity, which is why the slot is read from `begin` and not from `track=`: that field is emitted from `midiChannel`, not a track index.
